_note: Leadership changes after the Factbook's final edition (Feb 2026), verified 12 October 2026.

rows.Head of government: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) (sworn in 17 February 2026)
rows.Note: BNP-led alliance won 212 seats, a two-thirds majority, in the February 2026 election.

rows.Head of government: Prime Minister Balendra (Balen) Shah, Rastriya Swatantra Party (since 27 March 2026)
rows.Note: RSP won 182 of 275 House of Representatives seats in the March 2026 election.

rows.Head of state: President Min Aung Hlaing (elected by parliament in early April 2026)
rows.Note: Chosen under the military-drafted constitution after the 2025–26 elections; the armed forces retain a dominant role.

rows.Head of government: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Bhumjaithai Party (re-elected by the House on 19 March 2026)
rows.Note: Bhumjaithai won 193 of 500 seats in the 8 February 2026 election and leads a coalition.

rows.Head of government: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Labour (since 20 July 2026)
rows.Note: Keir Starmer announced his resignation in June 2026; Burnham was elected Labour leader in July.
Ali Khamenei was killed in an airstrike on 28 February 2026 at the start of the 2026 Iran war; the Assembly of Experts chose his son as successor.
